solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ringo at once adjusted embracing grand group

indicators.note: embracing means the rearranged letters hug the other piece inside them
adjusted says the letters of the three words before it are put into a new order

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Ringo and his bandmates suddenly rearranged themselves around some big-name group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges RINGOATONCE, and 'embracing' puts G inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of worshippers in a church is an assembled body of people, a kind of group.

clue.text: Skipped, bothered about exercise

indicators.note: about means the first word's synonym goes around the second's

parts.note: if you were bothered about something, you cared
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone skipped the gym, too bothered about the exercise involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipped' looks like 'missed out', matching the gym-dodging picture; it means hopped about.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or leap about playfully, so capered is a past-tense synonym of skipped.

clue.text: Winds up from opposite directions around ship

indicators.note: around means the two compass letters sit either side of the vessel

parts.note: north, written N, is one of two opposite compass points
south, written S, is the opposite compass point to north
an ark is a ship, as Noah's was

explanation.surface: Gusts blowing from both sides at once surround a vessel at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds up' looks like weather; it means annoys. 'around' puts ARK between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark someone is British slang for irritating them, the same as winding them up.

clue.text: Tries a second time, a learner getting practice

parts.note: to rehear a case is to try it again in court
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A driving student who tries everything twice gets plenty of practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' is the legal sense: a judge rehearing a case tries it again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before the real one.

clue.text: Rifles secure, having been cocked

indicators.note: cocked means turned up or tilted, so the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: snug means safe and secure, tucked in

explanation.surface: The rifles are made safe, even though they have been cocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been cocked' turns SNUG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rifles are a kind of firearm, and guns is the general term for them.

clue.text: Cut handle on safe to get valuables

indicators.note: Cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to handle someone is to treat them
safe can mean sure, as in a safe bet

explanation.surface: A thief cuts the handle off a safe to get at the valuables inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' looks like a door handle on the safe, but it is the verb, as in handling someone well.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a hoard of precious things, a collective word for valuables.

clue.text: Old judge to make a speech

parts.note: to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: An elderly judge rises to address the court.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address, a synonym for speaking publicly.

clue.text: He drives Morris's first old Traveller, not posh!

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Morris's
not means the posh letter is left out of the traveller's word

parts.note: a tourist is a traveller on holiday
U is upper-class, the posh sense from 'U and non-U'

explanation.surface: Someone drives an old Morris Traveller, a classic car that is anything but posh.
explanation.walkthrough: The Morris Traveller was a British estate car. 'not' drops U from TOURIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is a person who drives a car, so 'he drives' describes one.

clue.text: Robber, outlawed we hear, one time

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said aloud and a like-sounding spelling used

parts.note: something outlawed is banned
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a robber was outlawed once upon a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns BANNED into its sound-alike BAND, then I and T follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed robber, especially one in a lawless gang.

clue.text: Topless, move rhythmically on pole, maybe

indicators.note: on means the trimmed piece sits after the measure in this across answer

parts.note: a perch is an old measure of length, also called a pole or rod

indicators.note: Topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to dance is to move rhythmically

explanation.surface: Perhaps a topless pole dancer is moving to the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' and 'pole' set up a pole-dancing scene, but a pole is a unit of length, equal to a perch. 'Topless' cuts DANCE to ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for perhaps, so it can replace maybe.

clue.text: Square described by Pythagoras?

indicators.note: described by means the letters lie inside the name, as if drawn within it

explanation.surface: Was a square one of the figures described by Pythagoras?
explanation.walkthrough: Pythagoras makes you think of geometry, so 'Square' looks like a shape, but here it is a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: An agora was the public square or marketplace of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Part of Clytemnestra's calling for deceitful character

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Clytemnestra's trade was that of a treacherous schemer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'for', which is only a link word; the definition is 'deceitful character'. Clytemnestra murdered her husband Agamemnon in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a dishonest rogue, a scoundrel who cheats or tricks people.

clue.text: Unearthly rock, Queen do it as arranged outside

indicators.note: outside means the reordered letters wrap around the royal abbreviation
arranged says the letters of 'do it as' are put in a new order

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen tells someone to deal with an unearthly rock just as it has been arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' looks like a link word but belongs in the fodder for 'arranged'.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a rocky body orbiting the Sun, a rock from beyond the Earth.

clue.text: Sleep then wake up, say, by day's opening

indicators.note: opening takes just the first letter of day's
say means the word is spoken and a like-sounding spelling used

parts.note: to rouse someone is to wake them up

explanation.surface: Doze off, then wake up at the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives ROWSE, the sound of ROUSE, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To drowse is to doze or be half asleep, so it works as a verb meaning sleep.

clue.text: Theatrical actor with pie splattered

indicators.note: splattered says the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor gets a custard pie splattered in his face for comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link; 'splattered' rearranges ACTORPIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic means overly dramatic, as in opera, so it is a synonym of theatrical.

clue.text: One pulls out all the stops for performance!

definitions.text: One pulls out all the stops for performance!

parts.words: One pulls out all the stops for performance
parts.note: read literally, this is a musician drawing out every stop knob on a pipe organ to play a piece

explanation.surface: Someone throws everything into a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulls out all the stops' means makes every effort, but organ stops are the knobs that bring in sets of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the organ draws the stops to bring in its ranks of pipes.

clue.text: Supporter showing sense after a game

indicators.note: after means the meaning piece comes after the first two pieces

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist of something is its sense or meaning

explanation.surface: A fan shows good sense after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is only a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist defends a cause or person in argument, so is a supporter of it.

clue.text: Impress producing large port

explanation.surface: Making a strong impression creates a large port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' here means force into naval service, not make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai is to force someone into service, like impressing sailors; it is also China's great port city.

clue.text: Quiet bird, tense, with timid exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the timid word forms the outside around the other pieces

parts.note: timid means shy
a teal is a small duck
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A quiet bird, nervous and timid on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' could be the adjective for the bird, but it is the definition, meaning furtive.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means moving quietly and secretly so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: One's thrown to get a day off!

definitions.text: One's thrown to get a day off!

parts.words: One's thrown to get a day off
parts.note: read literally, something tossed to win a holiday; really it is the British idiom for faking illness to skip work

explanation.surface: Something is hurled to earn a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw a' plus this word is British slang for pretending to be ill to miss work.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a fake sick day off work is one you 'throw'.

clue.text: Had a row?

parts.note: read as an argument, but row rhymes with go and means rowing on water

explanation.surface: Did they have a quarrel?
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel (rhymes with cow); it means rowing a boat (rhymes with go).
explanation.definitionFit: To row is to travel by oar, which is going out in a small vessel on the water.

clue.text: Dirty, empty squalid house

indicators.note: empty means the inside of dirty is cleared out, leaving its ends

parts.note: squalid means filthy and nasty

explanation.surface: A filthy, abandoned and squalid house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a building; it means a royal family line, as in the House of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house is a ruling family line, which is what a dynasty is.

clue.text: Following check, preparing for attack and winning

indicators.note: Following means the second piece is written after the chess letters

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
arming is getting weapons ready to attack

explanation.surface: After putting the opponent in check, a chess player readies an assault and wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning' means attractive, as in a winning smile, not victorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning can mean delightful or engaging, as in a winning smile, the same as charming.

clue.text: Turned up, say, obscure insect

indicators.note: Turned up means the pieces are read from bottom to top in this down answer

parts.note: EG, for example, is a way of writing say
dim means faint or obscure

explanation.surface: Some vague, unclear insect has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses EGDIM in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny biting fly, a kind of insect.

clue.text: Party approaching Sea World

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
the main is an old word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A party is being held close to the Sea World theme park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea World' reads as the theme park; split it. 'approaching' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a realm or sphere of activity, someone's world.

clue.text: Bowl and a new period's over

indicators.note: over means the pieces are turned upside down in this down answer

parts.note: an era is a period of time; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A fresh period is over and a bowl is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses ANERA. 'Bowl' is a stadium, as in the Hollywood Bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is an amphitheatre or stadium, a sporting or performing venue.

clue.text: Strong draught beer with good head

indicators.note: head means the good letter goes at the top of this down answer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A strong draught beer with a good frothy head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draught' looks like a beer on tap; it means a current of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale is a very strong wind, a powerful draught of air.

clue.text: Incredibly long, incredibly ancient description initially

definitions.text: Incredibly long, incredibly ancient description initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: An account that is unbelievably lengthy and unbelievably old.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Homer's epic is long and ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War is extremely long and nearly three thousand years old.

clue.text: Shandies drunk around time finally creating intoxication

indicators.note: around means the mixed letters go round the final letter
drunk says the letters of the drink are scrambled
finally takes the last letter of time

explanation.surface: Drinking shandies over time ends in being tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: A shandy is a British drink of beer mixed with lemonade. 'drunk' rearranges SHANDIES and 'around' puts it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Headiness is the state of being heady, dizzy or giddy from drink.

clue.text: Intern a type I fancy, here?

definitions.text: Intern a type I fancy, here?

indicators.note: fancy means the letters are worked into an elaborate new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses about locking away a type of person they rather like.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a prison is where you intern someone. 'Intern' looks like a junior worker; it means imprison.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison is a place where people are interned, locked up.
